Hoare partition

Rearrange the elements in the array segment `[lo, hi]` around a pivot taken from the segment and return an index `split` so that, on termination, every element in `[lo, split]` is `<= pivot` and every element in `[split + 1, hi]` is `>= pivot`.

Three-way partition invariants

State the invariants in the three-way partition problem:

- after each loop iteration
- upon termination
cards.answer:
After each iteration:

- `[0, lt)`: known < pivot
- `[lt, i)`: known == pivot
- `[i, gt]`: unknown
- `[gt + 1, n)` known > pivot

At termination `i == gt + 1` and:

- `[0, lt)`: known < pivot
- `[lt, gt]`: known == pivot
- `[gt + 1, n)`: known > pivot

Convert between closed and half-open intervals

Represent the same set of integer indices using a closed interval and a half-open interval.
cards.answer:
- Closed to half-open: `[l, r] -> [l, r + 1)`
- Half-open to closed: `[l, r] -> [l, r - 1)`

Comments:

- Closed to half-open can in principle overflow with `r + 1`
- Half-open to closed is undefined if `l == r` (empty half-open interval)

cards.question:

cards.answer: `length = r - l + 1`

cards.question:
Length of a half-open interval

Compute the number of integers in `[l, r)`
cards.answer: `length = r - l`

cards.answer: Empty if `l == r`, undefined if `l > r`.

cards.question:
Overlap of closed intervals

Determine whether `[a, b]` and `[c, d]` share at least one point
cards.answer: The intervals overlap if `a <= d && c <= b`, or equivalently if `max(a, c) <= min(b, d)`

cards.question:
Overlap of half-open intervals

Determine whether `[a, b)` and `[c, d)` share at least one point
cards.answer:
The intervals overlap if `a < d && c < b`, or equivalently
if `max(a, c) < min(b, d)`

cards.question:
Disjoint half-open intervals

Determine whether `[a, b)` and `[c, d)` are disjoint.
cards.answer: The intervals are disjoint if `(b <= c || d <= a)` (if one interval is completely before the other)

cards.question:
Union of overlapping intervals

Produce the union of overlapping...

- Closed intervals `[a, b]` and `[c, d]`.
- Half-open intervals `[a, b)` and `[c, d)`.
cards.answer:
- `[min(a, c), max(b, d)]`
- `[min(a, c), max(b, d))`

- Closed intervals `[a, b]` and `[c, d]`.
- Half-open intervals `[a, b)` and `[c, d)`.
cards.answer:
- `[max(a, c), min(b, d)]`
- `[max(a, c), min(b, d))`

cards.question:
Interval adjacency

State the adjacency (intervals are consecutive with no overlap) condition for:

- closed intervals `[a, b]` and `[c, d]`
- half-open intervals `[a, b)` and `[c, d)`
cards.answer:
- Closed intervals: `b + 1 == c`
- Half-open intervals: `b == c`

- Last occurrence of `x`:

cards.question:
Existence in terms of bounds

State conditions for existence of `x` in an array...

- In terms of `lower_bound(x)`
- In terms of `upper_bound(x)`
- Relationship of `lower_bound(x)` and `upper_bound(x)`
cards.answer:
`x` exists in an array if:

- `lower < n` and `arr[lower] == x`
- `upper > 0` and `arr[upper - 1] == x`
- `lower < upper` (`x` is absent if `lower == upper`)

cards.question:

- Successor of `x`:
cards.answer:
- Predecessor of `x`: `lower_bound(x) - 1`
- Successor of `x`: `upper_bound(x)`

Comment: both answer subject to bounds checking.
